exit_trigger: Any integrity question emerges about management, accounting or disclosure; Scuttlebutt work turns up negative signals from customers, former employees or competitors; A fresh 15-point evaluation scores below 11; R&D effectiveness or the margin trend deteriorates (margin gains reverse without documented cost-engineering reasons); Equity issuance or accelerating dilution that cancels shareholders' benefit from growth; The original purchase proves to have been a mistake in assessing management or the competitive position
rationale: I own these shares, a 50-share position bought at $15.18 and now about 5% ahead after 189 days. A short holding period is not what decides the question. The numbers I can see are impressive: five-year revenue growth of 41.4%, a 37.1% operating margin, no debt against equity, and R&D at 11.5% of revenue. But I never buy on numbers alone, and I have no evidence in front of me on management integrity, scuttlebutt, or depth of management. Missing evidence is not evidence of a flaw, so I see no trigger to sell and I will not chase a price-driven exit. Neither can I add to the position until the integrity and scuttlebutt work is done. I hold, with low confidence, and I get on with that work. A P/E of 7.7 interests me only as a question of why the market is so cautious, and the answer must come from the people and the products.
